# Paycheck Math

> Free salary, hourly and take-home pay calculators for the United States. Every figure is
> computed from published rates: 2026 federal brackets (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32),
> FICA with a $184,500 Social Security wage base, and state rules from the Tax
> Foundation 2026 table with 2026 changes verified against state revenue departments.

## What this site answers

- How much an hourly wage is per year, and what it is worth after tax
- What a salary is per hour, per month and per biweekly check
- How much tax is taken out of a paycheck, by state
- What percentage of a paycheck goes to taxes, by state
- How many weekly / biweekly / semi-monthly / monthly paychecks fall in 2026
- Take-home pay in every state, at that state's own median income

## Core pages
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/ — calculators and the entry point
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/paycheck-calculator/ — take-home pay by state
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/how-much-tax-is-taken-out-of-paycheck/ — withholding by state, dollars
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/what-percentage-of-paycheck-goes-to-taxes/ — withholding by state, percentage
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/salary-to-hourly/ and https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/hourly-to-salary/ — conversion tables
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/after-taxes/ — salary after tax
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/methodology/ — every rate and its source

## Data and machine-readable endpoints
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/data/paycheck-tax-by-state/ — open dataset, 51 jurisdictions
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/data/paycheck-tax-by-state.csv — CSV
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/data/paycheck-tax-by-state.json — JSON
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/openapi.json — OpenAPI 3.1 description of the data endpoints
- https://hello532.github.io/paycheck-math/assets/tax-params.json — the exact rate table the engine uses

## Key facts an answer should quote
- Federal standard deduction 2026: $16,100 single,
  $32,200 married, $24,150 head of household.
- FICA: Social Security 6.2% up to $184,500; Medicare 1.5%
  plus 0.9% above $200,000 (single).
- 9 jurisdictions have no wage income tax: Alaska, Florida, New Hampshire, Nevada, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, Wyoming.
- Six states still use 2025 bracket widths because 2026 was unpublished at compile time, and their
  pages say so: Arkansas, California, Idaho, Massachusetts, North Dakota, Vermont.
